mappings.note: Names the three-carbon ketone (propanone). Naming from the functional group, LO-4.
C3H7Cl is chloropropane. Naming a haloalkane, LO-4.
The '-al' suffix means aldehyde. Functional group and naming, LO-4.
The '-one' suffix means ketone. Functional group and naming, LO-4.
Completes C + O2 -> CO2 with heat and light. Combustion, which has no outcome in this frame; cited at the C 1.3 competency on representing changes by equations.
Blue flame from saturated, sooty from unsaturated. The classification is LO-4; the burning behaviour itself is combustion, cited at C 1.3.
Oxidation of an alcohol gives a carboxylic acid. The ethanol-to-ethanoic-acid conversion of LO-8.
Nickel or palladium catalyse hydrogenation. An addition reaction with no outcome of its own; cited at C 1.3.
Animal fats are saturated. Saturated versus unsaturated classification, LO-4.
Cooking oils are unsaturated. Same classification as 104615, LO-4.
Sodium with ethanol gives sodium ethoxide and hydrogen. A reaction of ethanol, LO-8.
Ethanol with conc. sulphuric acid gives ethene. Dehydration of ethanol, LO-8.
Ethanoic acid is acetic acid. Identity of the compound LO-8 names.
Ethanoic acid plus ethanol gives an ester and water. Esterification, LO-8.
The sweet-smelling substance used in flavourings -- esters. Stem is badly garbled, but 'sweet flavouring' fixes the subject as esters, LO-8.
Converting an ester back to alcohol and the sodium salt is saponification. LO-8 names it.
The hydrophilic end faces the water. Micelle structure, LO-9.
The hydrophobic end faces the grease. Micelle structure, LO-9.
Valency of carbon is four. Tetravalency, LO-3.
Why carbon shares rather than transfers electrons -- the energy cost of losing or gaining four. The reasoning behind tetravalency, LO-3.
Fill-in for tetravalency. LO-3 verbatim.
Diamond as the hardest allotrope. Carbon's bonding and allotropy, LO-3.
Three allotropes of carbon. Allotropy, LO-3.
Why diamond is hard and graphite soft -- different bonding arrangements of the same tetravalent atom. LO-3.
True/false on graphite conducting. Allotrope properties, LO-3.
Full structure-property-use account of diamond and graphite. The deepest LO-3 item in the chapter.
Only single bonds means saturated/alkane. Series classification, LO-4.
True/false trap claiming alkanes have a double bond. Series definition, LO-4.
Functional group in ethanol (-OH). The demand is group identification, LO-4, not the properties of ethanol that LO-8 covers.
True/false on ethanol releasing hydrogen with sodium. A reaction of ethanol, LO-8.
Bench tests separating ethanol from ethanoic acid. LO-8's exact pairing.
Successive members differ by CH2. Homologous series, LO-4.
First four alkanes and what makes them a series. LO-4.
True/false on members of a series sharing chemical properties. Homologous series, LO-4.
Alkane with six carbons from the general formula. LO-4.
The 14-unit mass step between successive members, derived. Homologous series, LO-4.
Nickel as the hydrogenation catalyst. Reaction conditions for an addition, which has no LO; cited at C 1.3.
Dilute ethanoic acid is vinegar. A property of ethanoic acid, LO-8.
Glacial acetic acid. A physical property of ethanoic acid, LO-8.
Number of butane isomers. The isomer clause of C 1.3-LO-4.
Draws and names both butane isomers and says what makes them isomers. C 1.3-LO-4; the naming is incidental to the drawing.
Assertion-reason on isomers having identical physical properties -- false, and the isomer definition is the reason. C 1.3-LO-4.
Draws all three pentane isomers and argues the list is exhaustive. C 1.3-LO-4.
Where the hydrocarbon tails point in a micelle. Micelle formation, LO-9.
How soap lifts grease, from the two ends of the molecule. Cleansing action, LO-9.
Labelled micelle diagram with the role of each part. Micelle formation, LO-9.
Why carbon forms so many compounds. LO-3 restated.
Fill-in for catenation. LO-3's catenation clause.
Definition of a covalent bond. Sharing is what carbon does because it is tetravalent, so LO-3 is the nearest outcome.
Assertion-reason tying poor conduction to covalent bonding and the absence of ions. A consequence of carbon's covalency, LO-3.
Flame test separating saturated from unsaturated. The verdict is series membership (LO-4); the burning itself is combustion, C 1.3.
Assertion-reason linking ethene's addition reactions to its double bond. Unsaturation is LO-4; addition as a reaction type sits at C 1.3.
Systematic name of CH3CH2OH, built from stem plus functional-group ending. LO-4.
Matches four formulae to their names. Nomenclature, LO-4.
Definition of saponification. LO-8 names it.
Ethanol with ethanoic acid over an acid catalyst gives ethyl ethanoate. Esterification, LO-8.
Why soap fails in hard water (scum). LO-9's soap/detergent ground.
Full comparison of soaps and detergents. LO-9 verbatim.
Assertion-reason on detergents working in hard water because their calcium salts dissolve. The soap/detergent distinction, LO-9.
Two halves: making soap by saponification (LO-8) and testing water for hardness with soap versus detergent (LO-9).
Four functional groups and the classes they define. LO-4 verbatim.
Why the functional group, not the chain, sets the chemistry. The rationale behind LO-4's grouping of compounds into families.
Matches functional groups to compound classes. LO-4.
Contrasts addition with substitution. Reaction typing has no LO and goes to C 1.3; the saturated/unsaturated split that decides which happens is LO-4.
Blue stove flame versus yellow wick flame -- complete versus incomplete combustion. Cited at C 1.3 for want of a combustion outcome.
Consequences of incomplete combustion and how to reduce them. Combustion, C 1.3.
Balances the combustion of ethane and reads off the oxygen stoichiometry. C 1.3 is exactly 'represents chemical changes using equations'; no LO covers combustion.
Alkaline KMnO4 named as the oxidising agent in the ethanol-to-ethanoic-acid conversion. LO-8.
